utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: Good afternoon for everybody. Could the Registrar please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon. This is Case Number IT-97-24-T, the Prosecutor versus Milomir Stakic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: The appearances, please, for the parties.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Nicholas Koumjian, Ann Sutherland, and Ruth Karper for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Branko Lukic and John Ostojic for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: Thank you. Unfortunately, Judge Schomburg is still not available to sit in the courtroom this afternoon as he remains unwell. Rule 15 bis of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence permits two Judges of the Chamber to sit for up to five days in the absence of the Judge. Therefore, Judge Argibay and I will again be sitting this afternoon under Rule 15 bis. Following on from the discussion last night on the remaining witnesses for the Defence case, I have a few additional questions. In the light of the documents received from the Defence, can we please go into private session to discuss the names of the witnesses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Travar. The Bench would like to remind you that you are still under the solemn declaration to tell the truth in this courtroom. Please be seated.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: Before we start testimony of Mr. Travar, I would like to pay attention to the party that on the page 73 last transcript, line 16, the mistake was -- has been made. In the line 16, it is mentioned that Judge Schomburg is in the courtroom. Maybe his spirit was here, but physically Judge Schomburg was absent from the courtroom. Now, before I give the floor to the Defence, I would like to put some additional questions to Mr. Travar from the Bench.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: Mr. Travar, does the term "option 2 government" mean anything?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Government? Are you saying government? No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: It's -- you know, it relates to the shadow government, to the legitimate-elected government, in Prijedor Municipality.

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Travar. Now, yesterday you mentioned about the chain of command existed in the sphere of military -- in the military sphere and the sphere of police, in the sphere of civilian authorities. Can you tell us, what will be -- what was the chain of command in military sphere?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, there was the general staff at the level of the republic. Then there were subordinate units, those were corps commands, and lower formations. I believe that this was the hierarchy, and it ended with brigades or lower units. I'm not sure about the military structure, but I know that there was a general staff, that there were corps commands, Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. and lower formations at the level of brigades and such units.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: Did the Ministry of Defence existed in Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there was a Ministry of Defence. It was the civilian organ in charge of military issues with the government of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: And Colonel Arsic, whom he did report to?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that he reported to the corps command. And at that time, I don't know who the corps commander was. I believe that it was General Talic, but I'm not sure whether he was the corps commander at that time. In any case, Colonel Arsic reported to the corps command.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Travar. And what was the chain of command in police sphere?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the police, there was a ministry, the ministry of the police. There were public security centres and public security stations. So the ministry, the centre, and the stations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: And Simo Drljaca, whom he did report to?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: He reported directly to the chief of the public security centre which was headquartered in Banja Luka. I believe at that time, the chief of the centre in Banja Luka was Stojan Zupljanin. I'm not sure, but this is what I believe to be the case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: And what was the chain of command in your sphere? Who was your immediate superior? Who did you report to?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Kovacevic. He was the president of the Executive Board.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: And who were your subordinates?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said yesterday that my secretariat consisted of four departments. There was the department for economy, the department for budget and finances, the department for agriculture and forestry, and the department for service industries. The head of the department for economy was Mr. Grahovac, Zeljko Grahovac. The head of budget and finances was Mr. Nevenka Lucar. The department for agriculture and forestry was headed by Mr. Milosavljevic. And finally, the service industries department, I can't remember whether it was Mr. Aco Milic or not. I'm not sure. He was an inspector in charge of education and schools. I don't know who his assistant was. I don't know what his name was, but I believe it was Mr. Aco Milic. He was in charge of education and school system, and he was one of my assistants.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: Who did Dr. Kovacevic report to?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Executive Board is a body of the Municipal Assembly. That means that he reported to the Municipal Assembly and to the president of the Municipal Assembly, and that was Mr. Stakic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: And who did Mr. Stakic, as president of the Municipal Assembly, report to, on the republican level?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can try and explain, but I'm not sure whether I will be right. The Municipal Assembly and the president of the Municipal Assembly reported directly to the president of the assembly at the republican level which was a legislative body. I'm talking about the assembly of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and the president of the Municipal Assembly should report to the president of the Assembly of Serbian Republic. Executive Boards were bodies which were appointed by the assembly, and they reported to the assemblies. But their line of communication with the republican organs did not go via the assembly, but via the government and the sectoral ministries. I'm not familiar with the organisation of the state administration, but I believe that this is how these bodies functioned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: And at that time, who was the president of the Assembly of Serbian Republic?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that it was Mr. Krajisnik.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: Did you -- may I ask you the following question: Did Dr. Stakic reported to president of the Republic, Radovan Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether he reported directly to the president. I believe that he did. There was such a line of communication, but I cannot say whether this was regulated in formal and legal terms, whether he was supposed to report directly to the president of the republic. But I believe since everybody reported at the end of the day to the president of the republic, I believe that Dr. Stakic was no exception. Here, when I say that, I'm not sure whether he reported directly to him, but I believe that he did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: Have you heard that at that time, a rift occurred between Madam Plavsic and Radovan Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that it would happen at that time. It occurred later on, I believe. I don't know whether it happened in 1992. I can't say that for a fact. But later on, particularly in 1997, when Mrs. Plavsic dissolved the assembly, this is the period of time that I'm familiar with, I know that she broke off with the SDS, that she dissolved the assembly, and a new government was elected. But this was in the year 1997. And as for the rift between her and Mr. Karadzic, I wouldn't be able to tell you when that happened. I just don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: What side did Dr. Stakic take in this rift?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know. I can't tell you. In 1997, I didn't have any contacts with Dr. Stakic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: What was the relationship between Dr. Stakic and Biljana Plavsic?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't tell you that they had contacts, that they had good relations, because I don't know. Your Honour, I don't know what their relationship was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: Were you ever a member of SDS?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was, but I don't remember the date when I became a member.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: Approximately?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know how the SDS party booklet was handed to me. It was Mr. Simo Miskovic who brought it to my house. I didn't remember that when I gave my statement, but it was my wife who reminded me that Mr. Miskovic, who was my neighbour, came to my house and brought the party booklet to me. I don't know exactly when it was. I believe it was in late 1992 or early 1993. But I am not a hundred per cent sure. I believe that this information exist on the party records.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: And why did you decide to become a party member, I mean an SDS party member?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was not my decision. At that time the SDS was some kind of a movement, and I believe that most Serbians supported the SDS. Mr. Miskovic told me that it was not appropriate for me to hold a post without being a member of the SDS because this might result in some problems when people are elected to certain posts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: Mr. Travar, isn't it true that it was part of political culture in the Republika Srpska that the principal political decisions on the most important issues were initially taken by SDS leadership; and later on, these decisions were implemented by the civilian police and military bodies in accordance with their powers and competence?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot confirm that this was the case. But I'm sure that important decisions were taken at party meetings. I cannot say whether these decisions were influential with other bodies who -- which were supposed to implement them. But in any case, the influence of the SDS at that time was significant, and the election result showed that the SDS was the most powerful political option and party within the Serbian body of the population.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: Mr. Travar, isn't it true that the person couldn't be appointed to an important post without prior recommendation of SDS?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Generally speaking, that was the rule, although there were cases at the beginning that people were appointed to certain posts without being members of the party. At the time when I was appointed -- I was not a member of the party when I was appointed the secretary of the secretariat for economy and service industries.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: Mr. Travar, who did belong to the SDS Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. leadership in Prijedor Municipality? Can you name the most influential political figures in Prijedor Municipality.

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm afraid that I won't be able to do it for that period of time. I can't tell you who was the most influential person at that time. But the deputies on behalf of the SDS were Mr. Srdjo Srdic and Mr. Timarac. I don't know his first name. Those were two deputies in the assembly. Simo Miskovic was the president of the SDS at that time. And I would also like to mention Dragan Savanovic, who I believe was a member of the mixed assembly. He was a president of a standing committee or the group of SDS deputies. And during the first multiparty elections, Dr. Kovacevic, Mico Kovacevic, and Mr. Stakic, as the vice-president of the Municipal Assembly, were elected. And I believe, and it goes without saying, that he became the vice-president of the assembly because he was a member of the SDS. I can't remember any more names. There was another man who was the first president, but I can't remember his name. No, I can't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: And what were the most important official, governmental posts in Prijedor Municipality?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: In which period of time?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: In 1992. We are talking about 1992 period.

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Stakic, as the president of the Municipal Assembly; Mr. Kovacevic, as the president of the Executive Board; Mr. Savanovic, the vice-president. You're referring only to the Municipal Assembly, not to the police structures. And all the members of the Executive Board, including myself as the secretary of one of the secretariats. Mr. Stakic, Mr. Savanovic was his deputy. Mr. Kovacevic was the president of the Executive Board. Mr. Bosko Mandic was his deputy. And then there were the secretaries who were appointed to the Executive Board. I as a secretary of the secretariat for the economic affairs. Pavicic, Budimir, Boro Babic, the head of the tax administration. There was the secretary for general administration, and the secretary was Mr. Svetozar Petrovic. And there was also Mr. Banovic, who was the head of communal services secretariat. I don't know whether I've managed to mention all the secretaries and all the secretariats, but in any case, there must be a decision on appointment of all these people.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Travar. You have an excellent memory. And can you remember, did you receive orders from the republican level?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Personally I did not receive any orders from the republican level so that I never did get any such orders. I don't remember. No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: Mr. Travar, did you wear a uniform in --

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: For a short period of time, yes. During a short period of time when the Crisis Staff was in operation, but it was a very short time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: And can you explain me why did you wear a uniform.

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know why people wore it. Mr. Kovacevic I think told us as members of the Executive Board that we had to wear uniforms. And I wore it for about ten days or so, perhaps even less. I didn't think that as the secretary of that secretariat I should wear the uniform, and I took it off in no time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: Did Dr. Stakic wear a uniform?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: Did Dr. Stakic carry a weapon?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I believe he did carry a weapon for a while, at that time, late May, early June; that is, at the time of fighting in the area of the Prijedor Municipality.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: Did you start wearing uniforms when Crisis Staff was formed?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not straight away, not as of day one. But immediately after that, I mean, when the conflict started in the municipality of Prijedor. I think it was then that people started wearing uniforms.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: What were your relationship with Dr. Stakic?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was correct. I wasn't directly subordinated to Dr. Stakic because I was part of a body which accounted to the assembly, and we -- and in view of the kind of work that I did, even he couldn't order anything directly to my body, directly. He would have to go through the Executive Board so that we didn't meet or communicate frequently.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: Did you socialise with Dr. Stakic during working hours?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not in particularly. I didn't socialise. I'm a man who usually went home after working hours so that I didn't. I can't say that I socialised or that we spent together any time after the working hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Travar. I have no more questions. Judge Argibay? It's time for the Bench.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ARGIBAY
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I was thinking that the Defence was going to continue. I have a question that I couldn't find just now. So I don't have a question at the time. Please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: Okay. So the Defence will now continue with their line of questioning. Mr. Lukic, the floor is yours.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon once again, Mr. Travar.

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I will first go back to some of the questions you were asked today by His Honour Judge Vassylenko. I know that you never worked in a legislative body, that you only worked in the executive branch. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Were the members of the assembly -- of the Municipal Assembly, were the council of the municipality elected by direct vote, in elections that in a direct vote in which the inhabitants of the Prijedor Municipality participated?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you mean the councilmen by what you are saying?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know as a matter of fact, could the republican parliament dismiss any municipal councilmen?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it couldn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we then conclude that the municipal councilmen accounted to their electorate rather than the republican parliament?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I said in my testimony that I didn't really quite grasp the organisation of government, especially that part of the legislative authority. But yes, the assembly, the parliament, and the councilmen were responsible to their electorate. That is how it is. But when I was talking about this, I meant the communication which would be natural if it followed the line of legislative authority rather than the subordination, that somebody in the assembly, somebody in the Municipal Assembly, could issue orders to somebody in the municipal executive agency. That is what I was trying to explain.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In the spring and summer of 1992, we've established that you were not a member of the SDS. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think I was. I described it and said how I came by my membership card. But when was it entered in the records, what date is there, that is something that I don't know. And I never asked for that information, nor did I know it. All I know is when I quit the SDS. I know that date. But when I became its member, that, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Budimir wasn't a member of the SDS either at that time, the spring and summer of 1992?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. I think he wasn't a member either, but I'm not quite sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Is it true that Mr. Vojo Pavicic was not a member of the SDS Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. either? Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I do not know that, but I think that the majority of the Executive Board members who were elected were not members of the party.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Are you aware that Mr. Stakic was a member of the People's Radical Party Nikola Pasic?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know that the People's Radical Party Nikola Pasic participated in the elections in coalition with the SDS?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really do not know that. In 1992, I was completely outside any political developments, and I really don't know. I knew that there were those three ethnic parties were the HDZ, SDA, and the SDS. And yes, there was at that time also the party which had been founded by Mr. Ante Markovic. I know that it was one of stronger parties, if I may put it that way, but at least a party which was better known than others. But I didn't know of this people's -- what did you say it was called? People's Radical Party Nikola Pasic, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Well, feel free to tell me whenever you don't know something, just tell me that.

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You told us that your secretariat was responsible to the Municipal Assembly. Was the whole Executive Board responsible to the Municipal Assembly?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And did this -- was this responsibility of a political nature, whereas the secretariats were free in discharging their tasks?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the responsibility was reflected in the assessment of the performance of every individual body on the Executive Board. And that performance was assessed by the councilmen. The assembly could dismiss the whole Executive Board or any one of the secretariats if it had fallen below the expected performance or whatever.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did the Municipal Assembly meddle in the day-to-day work of individual agencies of the Executive Board?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now I will have only a few questions related to yesterday when you were answering the questions of the Chamber. I will quote the lines and pages, but don't get confounded by this, because it's only for the record. His Honour Judge Vassylenko asked you how could it be that Milomir Stakic be elected the vice-president of the Municipal Assembly, leaving aside various other more prominent, better-known people at the time. And you explained, at this 131st trial day of the transcript, page 10, line 21 onward, you said that it was an act of political compromise presumably. But let me just clear this up. Did the vice-president of the Municipal Assembly and the president of the same, could they be elected only from amongst the councilmen, from the municipal councilmen, or could somebody who wasn't?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that the vice-president, the vice-president had to be elected from amongst the councilmen in the Municipal Assembly. But I'm not quite sure about that. I think that is how it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: So only from amongst the ranks of the councilmen could the president and the vice-president be elected. I think that's how it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: My next question, perhaps you will know what the answer is, perhaps you won't. Page 11 of yesterday's transcript, line 25 continuing on the next page, you spoke about the moment when it was decided to establish Crisis Staffs. And you said, "I don't know why it happened, seeing that there were no combat operations in Prijedor." Are you aware perhaps if at that time there were any combat operations in Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think there were. But I said that the Crisis Staffs were set up on the basis of the position and instructions issued by the presidency. And pursuant to a decision on the organisation and work of the Crisis Staff, as laid down by the government of the Serb Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina. That is how I put it yesterday. But operations had already started in Bosnia and Herzegovina at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Likewise yesterday, page 47, line 10 onward, you mentioned a person whom you succeeded as the secretary of your secretariat. It is Mr. Milovan Dragic. What is Mr. Dragic's ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Serb, Serb ethnicity. His ethnicity is Serb.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I'd like to ask you something from the military area, and I believe it has to do with common knowledge. But once again, if you don't know, just tell me so. Are you aware that the military had the right to mobilise materiel if such a need arose?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So did the military have the legal right to mobilise the premises of the iron ore mine in Omarska?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the military had the right to mobilise all the materiel that the enterprises used, both private and those state-owned. I'm aware of that. And that is -- and they did that through the Ministry of Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And the Ministry of Defence, in the beginning of the conflict, was called the municipal secretariat of all people's defence of the Municipality of Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. Yes, it was the municipal secretariat for people's Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did the Crisis Staff -- was the Crisis Staff authorised to mobilise anything?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did the army and the police submit any reports directly in relation to mobilised things? Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. To the Executive Board or the Crisis Staff, they did not submit such reports. Whether they did submit such reports to their superior commands, that is something that I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Was the maintenance of public law and order and prevention of crime within the jurisdiction of the police? Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before, during that period, and after, it has always been within the competence of the law enforcement agencies and the police. That is their exclusive task.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In the spring and summer of 1992, did the municipal public prosecutor's office function in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there was the municipal public prosecutor. I think -- I think it existed. I'm not sure. I think -- I think it did.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In the spring and summer of 1992, did the municipal court function in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it did.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Was there the military police in Prijedor at the time?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there was.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did the military police -- was the military police's duty, to your knowledge, to look after the conduct of the army?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the civilian police looked after the maintenance of public law and order when it comes to the civilians and those others, I mean, not engaged individuals. And the military police was to keep order amongst the members of the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Could the civilian police arrest a soldier and place him under custody, civilian custody, or could a member of the army be arrested only by the military police and put him under military custody?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I tried to explain it in the previous question. That is, it was the exclusive competence of the military police to arrest and take under custody military persons.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In the spring and summer of 1992, if you know, were there any military prosecutor's offices in Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I assume there were. They existed throughout the war. Military prosecutor's offices, yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And those military prosecutor's offices, were they responsible for investigations and proceedings against -- and charges against members of Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. the army?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In the spring and summer of 1992, were there any military courts?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there were.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Were the military courts responsible for investigations and proceedings conducted against members of the military?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not know whether that was their task. But it sounds logical to me, because the military and the police were tried by military courts. I know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Could the Crisis Staff punish anyone for any crime?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Crisis Staff, and I said it yesterday, was not responsible either in legal terms or in any other way, because these structures, that is, the Ministry of the Interior, the prosecutor's office, and courts were responsible for proceedings and for the punishment of perpetrators for crimes. Rather, the Crisis Staff or any other municipal agencies under the then-legal regulations, that was not the responsibility of any municipal agency.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Could any municipal agency be responsible for the conduct of investigations, I mean some administrative agency in the municipality?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not know if the prosecutor's office, the public prosecutor's office in a municipality is a municipal agency. But when I talk about other municipal bodies, the Executive Board, secretariats, the Crisis Staff, the Municipal Assembly, they could not conduct any investigations or pronounce any punishments.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now we shall go back to the Crisis Staff. You told us that the Crisis Staff meetings were at times attended by representatives of the army and that it, by and large, happened when they were short of supply, whether it be materiel or clothing or... Through which civilian body -- which civilian body could they use as a channel to express their needs in materiel and the rest?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: They did it through the municipal secretariat for national -- for people's defence, that is, through the secretariat which was engaged in mobilising people and requisitioning all the materiel that they needed. But let me just explain something: Yesterday, when I spoke about this, they often came -- I mean, those meetings were not frequent, but they came. And when they came, those were problems which had to do with meeting the obligations put by the army to companies and the rest. That is, the army could, through the municipal secretariat, mobilise or requisition everything that it needed to conduct its operations in its area of responsibility. But the army -- the supply of military units went through their logistics basis. And whatever could not be delivered to them, they had contracts, especially when it comes to basic necessities, to foodstuffs, that the contracts between companies who at that time made bread and other things, that is, companies who supplied the town such as Velepromet or Energopetrol, who supplied the oil, they had contracts. And they as a rule never met their obligations, and then problems arose in those enterprises because they could not cover all the quantities that the army had taken and they interceded with us to help them to get the claims from the army because on the basis of the contracts, they were taking over those goods but were not paying for them. So this was part of the debate that we had with the army, and the part which refers to the number of people needed so that the companies of special interest for a municipality such as the supplies of the town with basic foodstuffs, that is, people who are responsible for the maintenance of the waterworks or the electric or the power-supply system, so that we could have them released from the army or exempt from their military duty and so that they could be sent back to work so that we could have more or less a normal life in the town. So they could issue out their normal duties in the town and the town could operate. So this was the gist of our discussions for which the military were invited to those meetings or when the military came, when those questions were to be discussed at the meetings.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Before the break, just one more question which is directly related to this: Did the army ever inform you how and for what it used this materiel and other things that were requisitioned?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Travar. Would it be a convenient time, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: It would a time for the break. Trial stays adjourned until 4.15.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: Please, Mr. Lukic, do continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I would like the usher now to show the witness Exhibit Number S180, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Travar, would you please turn to page 38, and at the beginning, at the very top of that page, you will see Item Number 22.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And the same pagination is in English, I guess.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Item 22, the bottom of the page reads: "The Crisis Staff of Prijedor Municipality issues the order to defend Serbian TO, Territorial Defence, Crisis Staff of Prijedor Municipality, which was dissolved," did you in May 1992 know about the existence of this Crisis Staff, that is, the Crisis Staff of the Serbian Territorial Defence of Prijedor Municipality?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were all sorts of Crisis Staffs, in companies and in other institutions, in local communes. There were a number of the bodies which called themselves "Crisis Staffs" or "staffs affiliated with various institutions." So I can't remember exactly what the Serbian Territorial Defence Crisis Staff was or what its purpose was.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Simo Miskovic speaks about a Crisis Staff that he headed. Do you know what Crisis Staff did Mr. Simo Miskovic talk about?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that is what I heard on the audiotape yesterday, but I don't know what Crisis Staff he was talking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now I would like the usher to show the witness the Exhibit Number S141, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Travar, could you please turn to page 44, to the very top of this page --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... In English version. I don't think that it's necessary for this document to be put on the ELMO, so Mr. Travar can read the first paragraph in this document, and I will ask him only one or two questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Kindly read the first paragraph --

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which starts with Momcilo Krajisnik?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Momcilo Krajisnik, we have to adopt these amendments. Who is in favour? Is anybody against? Abstaining? So these are the amendments to the constitution which have now been adopted. Discussion at the session held on 25th May 1992, the amendments to the law on national defence have been adopted. "Article 1: The law on national defence officially exempt 4/92 of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, in all the provisions of the law the words 'Territorial Defence' and 'armed forces' will be replaced by the words 'the army of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina.' "Article 2, paragraph 2, of the Article 10 is deleted. That is an article, and the paragraph which regulated something with regard to the Territorial Defence. "Article 3, and articles from 37 to 53 also relative to the Territorial Defence are hereby deleted. "Article 4, this law shall come into effect on eight days after its publication in the Official Gazette of the Serbian People of Bosnia and Herzegovina."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you please read the heading of this document on page 1 so we know what date we're talking about.

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the minutes of the session of the Assembly of the Serbian People of Bosnia and Herzegovina held on 12 May 1992 in Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Does this document say that the Territorial Defence of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina was abolished on the 12th May 1992?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is visible.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The 12 May 1992?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is what transpired from this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: After the establishment of the Crisis Staff, did you continue sitting in your office occupied by the secretary of the secretariat of economy for the municipality of Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, after the establishment, yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When there were no sessions of the Crisis Staff, did you continue discharging duties pertaining to your area of activity?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is what I did most of the time. I discharged the duties pertaining to my area of responsibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you remember that during the attack on Prijedor in the municipal building, there was a sniper shooting on that building, and that some windows were shattered and the glass was broken on some of the windows?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember, and then we moved. From then on, a few meetings were held in the basement of the municipal building. That was in late May or early June when these armed attacks started. And that is when we introduced the duty in those basement rooms which housed the early warning and information centre, or some sort of a service like that. That was in the basement of the municipal building.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Since you mentioned the 24-hour duty, can the usher show the witness the Document Number S106, please. In this document, this duty and introduction of this duty is mentioned. And the document also speaks about the tasks and information to be collected. I believe that this corresponds to something that you have already said, but can you please read this document, because I am going to have to ask you some questions connected with this document?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you want me to read the document aloud?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: "To all the economic subject, the introduction of a permanent operative duty: In keeping with the decision of the Crisis Staff of the Autonomous Region of Krajina, in all the municipalities of the Autonomous Region of Krajina, there is a duty. The purpose of introducing permanent operational duty by the Crisis Staff is to provide continuous monitoring of the situation in the civilian sector on the territory of the municipality; the giving of additional instructions for the implementation of conclusions, decisions, and orders of the Crisis Staff of the Prijedor Municipality; and that at any given moment outside working hours, government agencies and commercial bodies can be activated. "The permanent operational duty of the Crisis Staff shall be organised on the premises of the Municipal Assembly, and it will be on a 24-hour basis. Any important occurrences and events shall be reported to the following telephone number: 22-055. "In order to ensure that the main purpose of the introduction of permanent operational duty is achieved, it is vital that all commercial and social subjects inform the person on operational duty of any occurrence, event, problem, or situation in their immediate area. The duty Crisis Staff should mainly be informed of the following occurrences and events: "Problems in implementing decisions of the municipal Crisis Staff; incidents in the manufacturing process; absenteeism; intentional disruption of the manufacturing process and provision of services; inability to pay salaries; problems in the acquisition of raw materials and the sale of finished products; forcible migrations of population; arrivals of refugees; problems with supplies of groceries, medicines, and petrol and petroleum derivatives; outbreak of contagious diseases; cases of food and water poisoning; traffic disruptions; a need for an urgent meeting, et cetera. "The information should be provided by the director of the commercial enterprise or a person authorised by him. These persons must identify themselves and state the telephone number where they are calling from because only information provided in such a way shall be considered genuine. "We are also hereby informing you that it is your obligation to give your home and work telephone numbers to the Reporting Centre as well as the telephone number to be used when you are not at the numbers given to the information centre (this is relevant for the management of commercial enterprises). "President, Dr. Milomir Stakic."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In this document, do you see the issues that the Crisis Staff dealt with and for which it obtained information during the permanent-duty service?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this was more or less what the Crisis Staff did at that time. I already spoke about that, either yesterday or on the first day of my testimony. I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you sometimes have to be on duty in the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Were some other members of the Crisis Staff on duty as well?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there was a -- some sort of a rota. It was not just one person who was on duty. All the members of the Crisis Staff took turns, but I believe that myself and Mr. Budimir were there most often. We were the ones who were on duty most of the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did Mr. Milomir Stakic also have to take duty sometime?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was present downstairs. All the members of the Crisis Staff took turns according to the rota.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did Ostoja Marjanovic sometimes drop by to visit you while you were on duty? Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't remember. I cannot confirm that I remember. I know Mr. Ostoja Marjanovic. But whether he dropped by to those rooms at that time, I can't remember. I can't confirm that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well then. Thank you. Can you please tell us how long was this duty in place?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know. I believe that it lasted for some time. I can't give you the exact duration, whether it lasted up to the moment when the Crisis Staff stopped existing or whether its duty was abandoned earlier than that. I really can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We are no longer talking about this duty service. I would like to ask you something else, this time about the army and mobilisation of materiel and technical equipment by the army. As a Crisis Staff, could you issue an order to the army not to mobilise some materiel or technical equipment?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we couldn't do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You, as a Crisis Staff, could you issue an order to the army to return somebody from the army for that person to take the work obligation?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we couldn't issue such an order, but we could send a request for a certain number of people to be released from the army. And we did that through the department of national defence, and these were mostly my contacts with this particular secretariat when we had to send a request for the release of some people from the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And did the army always meet your requests, or sometimes, or never? What would you say?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was unfortunately only very rarely that they met our requests.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. During your testimony, you also mentioned the establishment of the intervention platoon, a joint intervention platoon, by the army and the police, and a decision was mentioned which was the Exhibit Number S79. In this decision, the Crisis Staff asked the army and the police to provide them with information on the people who were earmarked for this intervention platoon so that the Crisis Staff could approve the selection of these people. Do you remember whether the army and the police ever acted on this request and whether they provided the list of people to the Crisis Staff for their approval?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already said in my testimony that -- about this particular document. This document was an order for the establishment of the joint intervention platoon, and yesterday, I tried to explain what the motives were behind the decision made by the Crisis Staff. And the motive was exclusively to prevent the overall chaos and plunder of all the stores in town. And our discussion culminated at one of the sessions of the Crisis Staff at which we tried to ask from the police to restore order, that is, the police and the military -- police to restore order to the town. And that document was the result of that discussion. Later on, this document got the title "an order," although I'd like to say again that the Crisis Staff could not issue any orders to the police or to the military. However, this document was called an order to give it a somewhat bigger weight. Unfortunately, the police and the army never established any such intervention platoon. What they did in order to prevent those unfortunate incidents, we don't know, because they never submitted any reports to us so that we could find out what actions had been taken by them.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In the spring and summer of 1992, was there any unit, either an army unit or a police unit that would be commanded by the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, there was no such unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: As a member of the Crisis Staff, did you have a pass which enabled you to move about during the curfew?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we had to have a pass issued by the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now I would like to ask you something about the decisions relative to the proclamation of the abandoned property, state property.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I ask the usher to show you the document S192, please. And 193 at the same time, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Will you please be so kind as to read for us the first paragraph of article S -- in the document S192 entitled "Decision of proclaiming abandoned property property of the state."

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Article 1 of the decision says, "Abandoned property, real estate, and moveable items of persons who have left the territory of the Prijedor Municipality, and persons who participated in the armed rebellion, is temporarily proclaimed state property and the Prijedor Municipality becoming entitled to all possession rights."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: As you see from the text of the decision, does it refer to all the persons who left the territory of the Prijedor Municipality regardless of their ethnic origin?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yesterday when I spoke, I said that all the persons who had left the territory of the Prijedor had their property accorded the same status. And here it is proclaimed the state property -- I mean, it applies also to enterprises.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The decision shows that this is a provisional decision.

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, it is only temporarily proclaimed. That's what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And does this corroborate your view that this was done to protect this property?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I said yesterday I don't know if it's necessary for me to repeat it. I think that the purpose that there is on that behind all such acts was to protect this property against all further destruction because it was abandoned. And in order to attempt to prevent the further plundering of this property, that was the reason behind it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now I'd like to ask you to look at Document S193. From this decision, I'd like you only to read out the title.

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Decision on the allocation for temporary use of immoveable property that has been proclaimed state property."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So the use of real estate could be allocated to somebody temporarily?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is what the text of the decision says.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Was that the intent of the author of the decision, to temporarily allocate this property to somebody?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We've finished with this document. Thank you. Generally speaking, the property that was allocated for temporary use, was it protected to a much higher degree than the property which was not given to somebody for temporary use?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You've told us that you knew when Dr. Stakic was expelled from the Municipal Assembly, that he was no longer active in politics. Was Milomir Stakic called up after he quit the office of the president of the assembly? Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. But I did not speak about that yesterday. It is true that towards the end of 1992 or in early 1993, Dr. Stakic was relieved of his duty. But whether he was called up or not, that is something that I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you personally have an argument with Srdjo Srdic?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you could call it a conflict, but it was a conflict that originated on his side rather than on mine. But we were not on friendly terms.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: On the 27th of July, 1992, the Crisis Staff submitted its decisions to the Municipal Assembly for ratification. On the 24th of July, 1992, the last decision of the Crisis Staff was taken. Did these dates also mark the end of the Crisis Staff of the Municipal Assembly of Prijedor, if you remember?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not know if the dates are correct. I know that after the adoption of the decisions taken by the Crisis Staff, because this was in agreement with the instruction on the work and organisation of the Crisis Staffs, I know that after that, after those decisions were adopted, the Crisis Staff stopped functioning. It did not meet again. But I don't know -- I think it was late July, but I cannot recall the dates.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I understand that you cannot, and that is why I tried to prompt your memory. But as you tell us, it is exactly the end of July, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was sometime in midsummer when the Crisis Staff ceased functioning, and it was no doubt after these decisions were confirmed by the assembly, that is -- that, I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know where the fiercest fighting took place on the 30th of May, 1992, when Prijedor was attacked?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: That day, on that date, I was at home. That is, I wasn't in the municipal hall building, and I did not have precise information. I know that there was a lot of fighting in the town, that I could see smoke from the house that I used to live in at the time. So for those two days, I couldn't even make it to the municipal hall, and I was at home with my wife and daughter.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In 1991, you were called up for the 5th Kozara Brigade. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And during your tour of duty on the Slavonian front, was your house burgled, the house that you lived in?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So isn't it in 1991 already, anarchy and lawlessness set in in the Municipality of Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was called up on the 16th of September, 1991, and I was a member of the 5th Kozara, which at that time was on the Slavonian front. At that time, I was living at Dubicka Cesta. Namely, I already said I arrived in Prijedor in 1984 for the first time, and I was always subletting, that is, I was moving from one place to another. So at that time, I was living at Dubicka Cesta, which is a street leading to Dubica. And then sometime in October, I don't remember the exact date, that flat was burgled because my wife and daughter did not live there all by themselves and had instead moved to my cousin who had a house near Zitopromet. Since I was on the front, that is, I was away for a long time, I couldn't visit all that often.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now I'd like the witness to be shown Document S96. [In English] And if this document in B/C/S could be put on the ELMO, please. The bottom part, please, the signature part.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The image is pretty poor on the screen -- oh, it is much better now. Here it again says that Dr. Milomir Stakic is the signatory, but do you recognise his signature?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the first day when I was talking about signatures and identifying them, I confirmed two -- that is, three signatures. Dr. Stakic's wasn't one of those. But this signature here doesn't look like the signature on the document that I saw earlier so I cannot say whether this is Dr. Stakic's signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well. We won't be needing this document any more.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would also like to ask you something to do with stamps, whether in the Municipal Assembly and the Executive Board, were their stamps kept in the secretariats in the Executive Board or were they kept by the technical service? Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know. I don't know who kept them in these departments. But in my secretariat, every department has its own stamp with a number attached to it. So the budget had its own, the economy department had its own, so we had four stamps. And the stamp of the secretariat was with the secretary -- I mean, with my secretary in her room. But I -- how things were done in the Executive Board and the Municipal Assembly, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But can we also assume safely that every dignitary had to have a stamp with his number?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No. I don't know what do you -- what is it that you're asking me. I didn't have a seal of my own, a stamp of my own. I wasn't issued with one. It was issued to the technical service. The secretary kept it, the lady secretary kept it. And the stamps of individual departments were kept by the heads of these departments. At least, that is what I think happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In order to identify every service, its stamp should have a number that was on it, and that is how you identified them. Is that how it was?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that would be reasonable to have it that way, although I do not exclude the possibility that somebody else who did not come from a particular department to put this stamp and -- but in principle, everybody had his own stamp, and everybody was issued a stamp which had a number on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Travar. For the time being, I have no further questions. My learned friends from the Prosecution will take over, I guess.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: Please, Mr. Koumjian, the floor is yours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Mr. Travar, prior to testifying, did you review the interview you gave with the Office of the Prosecutor? Did you get any tapes or review any notes of that interview?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: In your position as the secretary of the economy, were you superior to the director of the Ljubija mine company?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Sir, you mentioned today that you knew Mr. Marjanovic, Ostoja Marjanovic. Mr. Marjanovic testified in this case on page 11.736 of the transcript, line 18: "I myself went to the secretary for the economy. I think it was Ranko Travar. In a manner of speaking, he was my superior minister in the municipality. So that was the reason why we had contacts throughout that period." Would you say, sir, that -- would you disagree with that characterisation by Mr. Marjanovic of your relationship?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not agree with it in no way because I couldn't be his superior, and I couldn't order Mr. Marjanovic anything. In my statement and in my testimony today - that is, not today but yesterday, I think - I said what was the role and the function of the secretariat for economy. So only in -- so it was only information, and there was no way in which we could order anything to any enterprise, least of all to the manager of the mine. And there is no order which I could issue to that effect.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you. And I believe you also testified that you didn't forward any orders to these enterprises from either the Prijedor or regional Crisis Staffs, the ARK Crisis Staff. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not remember if I did because documents which came from the Crisis Staff of the AR Krajina either went directly to enterprises, and those which came to the municipal hall came to the secretariat or the president of the Crisis Staff. It could have happened perhaps that I was on duty or that I was simply present, and therefore, perhaps, happened to see a document. But I really cannot say yes or no. I don't think that I ever gave any documents or that I received any documents directly as the secretary of the secretariat, except naturally those which had to do with the terms of reference of my secretariat.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Did you order private- and socially-owned enterprises to dismiss anyone who wasn't loyal to the Serbian state, or did you pass that order on?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I never ordered any such thing. I am quite confident that I never did that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Could the usher please distribute a document with the English ERN -- 65 ter number 235. It has the English ERN of 03024820. And the B/C/S ERN of P0054018. And Ms. Karper will take copies to the booth.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Mr. Travar, please take your time in reading this document to yourself. Perhaps so the record is clear, you could read it out loud, beginning with the heading. Could you, sir, please read it out loud slowly so that the interpreters can follow.

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Copy - extracts from the conclusions of the Krajina AR Crisis Staff. "At the session of the 3rd May 1992, of the Krajina Autonomous Region Crisis Staff adopted the following conclusion: "Production in all socially- and privately-owned enterprises shall follow wartime plans. "An appeal -- managers are called upon" -- I can't see what is this word "again" or "not." "Managers in Krajina enterprises are called upon to submit their wartime plans immediately to the Secretariat for National Defence - the National Defence Council - for analysis and approval. "Management positions in enterprises in the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina must be filled with people who are absolutely loyal. "President, Radoslav Brdjanin. "The authenticity of this copy is certified by Ranko Travar."

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Sir, I think the copies you have the stamp is extremely faint, and we will try to get a better copy of that. Having reviewed that document, Mr. Travar, how do you reconcile that with the testimony you have given about not giving any orders to private- or socially-owned enterprises or passing on orders from the ARK Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I confirmed here -- well, I don't know if I confirmed it. I do not know whether I had this document ever. This is the first time I see this document. I cannot recall that I had such a document. At that time, whether the -- the technical service or somebody in the Crisis Staff copied these fragments from the conclusions and I happened to be there as duty officer, I really don't know, and I cannot recall this. Yes, it does say "secretary, secretariat for economy, Ranko Travar," and says that I authenticate this copy, which means that this is a true copy of what has arrived from the AR Krajina's Crisis Staff. But I don't know if you have the original document perhaps.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: We'll try to get a better copy of what we have.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If possible to provide the witness with a copy with the signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'd appreciate not being interrupted in my cross-examination. Counsel can ask that after the examination. Obviously, we don't have a copy with the signature available at the moment. We don't have a copy with the signature. I will stipulate to that fact -- Excuse me, I will stipulate that we do not have a copy with the signature.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic. I ask you not to interrupt the OTP without the Court's permission.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, we have the right to object.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The counsel's microphone is off.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'll move on. But counsel has the right to object, but not to make arguments during my examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: Please, Mr. Koumjian.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Sir, when Dr. Stakic was replaced - you told us that was in late 1992 or early 1993 to the best of your recollection - you were replaced at the same time. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: During -- your relationship with Dr. Stakic, did you socialise with him yourself during 1992?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not too much. We met at work, but outside of working hours, very seldom. Almost never.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Did you see Dr. Stakic, Dr. Kovacevic, and Mr. Drljaca socialising, spending time together, outside of work?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't really move much around town. I told you I'm a family man, that is, I used every minute I had free to go and be with my family who were living privately so that I cannot confirm it confidently. All I know is that Dr. Stakic and Dr. Kovacevic were close friends because they worked together. And what I also knew from what my colleagues talked about was that Dr. Stakic and Mr. Drljaca at times shot pool together. But I wasn't present on such occasions, and I wasn't present when they met privately so that I cannot say whether and how much they socialised outside work. But I know that with Dr. Kovacevic, he often -- that he often saw Dr. Kovacevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you. Moving on to the National Defence Council, that was a body that you said you don't recall ever functioning. You don't remember that body. Is that still your testimony?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the interview with yourselves, I tried to refresh my memory with my colleagues, and I tried to remember what that body meant. And to this very day, believe me, I don't know what it was, what its function was. I saw the minutes from those meetings, and I know that I was there, and I am not disputing that fact. I attended a number of meetings by a number of different bodies because the issues that we dealt with, that is, my secretariat and me, was budget and finances, and that's why I was invited to a number of meetings in order to try and explain to the people what things could be funded from the budget.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: If the witness could be shown just S28, S60, and S90.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: I believe you've seen at least two of these documents already during your testimony, Mr. Travar, but these are three minutes of the meetings of the National Defence Council dated the 5th of May, the 15th of May, and the 29th of September. You told us during Mr. Lukic's examination that you were not a member of this body, but attended. In each of these minutes, you're listed as being in attendance. Can you explain why you attended all of these sessions of a body that you were not a member of?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already said that. I said that in the interview, and I say it before this Honourable Chamber. I attended because I was invited by the chairpersons of those bodies, and I would respond to those invitations, and I would attend those meetings. So every time I was invited to attend those meetings.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you. So the chairperson of the National Defence Council in Prijedor was Dr. Stakic. Would you have been invited by Dr. Stakic or by his secretary? Do you recall how you received the invitation?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember. I don't remember who invited me. In any case, my secretary would tell me that I was expected at one meeting or the other. It was usually my secretary who received those invitations.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Now, you told us that you never discussed at the Crisis Staff any police or military matters. You've also acknowledged that you were in attendance at this National Defence Council. Would you have recalled if you discussed military and police matters in a meeting with Dr. Stakic, Dr. Kovacevic, Mr. Drljaca, and others at the National Defence Council? In other words, did you discuss those matters in that body?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember whether I was involved in any of the discussions relative to the police or military issues. I really do not dispute the fact that I did attend those meetings. But after 11 years, it is very hard for me to remember any of the discussions. I did contribute to the discussions, but mostly relative to the issues that were within the purview of my secretariat. What I'm saying is that I only talked about those subject matters that I knew something about, that were close to me, because my motive is always to talk about those things that I understand and that I am familiar with, and nothing else.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you. I wasn't precise enough in my question. I didn't mean did you personally speak about them, about whether these topics were discussed at the meeting, the meetings that you attended of the National Defence Council with Mr. Drljaca and people from the military, such as Arsic, Zeljaja, and Pero Colic. Were those matters discussed? Did you discuss police and military matters? Did you discuss the conflict? When I say "you," were those subjects discussed in the meetings?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember. There were all sorts of discussions dealing with issues touching upon the work of the police and the army. But I can't remember the details of those discussions. But in any case, we tried to discuss the subject matters that were on the agenda that were proposed for the agenda of those meetings. Yesterday, I said that whenever I wanted to learn something from the police or the military, although at that time very few of us dared ask any of the military or police commanders about anything that pertained to the authority of the police, the answer would be more often than not that this is something where we shouldn't concern ourselves with. This was the job of the army, and the army had its line of reporting. So it was very difficult for any of us to obtain any information on what was going on from any member of the police or the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Sir, there was a curfew enforced in Prijedor in May and the summer of 1992. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there was a curfew.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: To refresh your recollection, looking at the minutes of the 5th of May, the second session of the National Defence Council, do you see that that order -- that that curfew was ordered in point number 6 by the National Defence Council in a meeting chaired by Dr. Stakic?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that under number 6.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Do you see in number 7 that at this meeting which took place with both the police and military commanders present that in point number 7, there is an order for persons and paramilitary formations possessing weapons to surrender them immediately? And it indicates they have until the 11th of May. Finally, that after this period, the relevant organs were start searches and seizures for any such weapons and ammunition and will apply the most rigorous sanctions. Do you recall now this discussion on the 5th of May, just a few days after the takeover of power?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I can't say either yes or no. I can't remember. I can see that this is what it says here, but I cannot remember the course of that discussion. Whether this is something that the Council for National Defence could do or not, I don't know. I cannot confirm that this is really what happened. I can see that this was confirmed at this session, but I can't remember who took part in the discussion on this issue. It says here "Milomir Stakic," but again, as I say, I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: When was the first time that you recall seeing or meeting with Dr. Stakic after the takeover on the 30th of April?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't say for a fact, but I believe that I saw him on that very morning in the municipal building. However, I'm not sure of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: To the best of your recollection, when was the first formal meeting that you had with him and others?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: It transpires from this that I was at this first meeting of the National Defence Council on the 5th of May. This transpires from this -- from these minutes. But if I didn't have this document in my hands, I would not be able to recall exactly when it was that I saw Dr. Stakic for the first time formally. I don't know whether this was the first time when I saw him formally, but on that morning, on the 30th, I believe that Dr. Kovacevic chaired the meeting of the Executive Board. On that morning, we were meeting in Mr. Kovacevic's office as far as I can remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Sir, isn't it true that once the Crisis Staff began to operate, the Executive Board was no longer functioning?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Crisis Staff replaced the Municipal Assembly. It could not stand in for the Executive Board at the same time. Now, how often did the Executive Board meet at that time, I can't remember. But judging by the position that the Crisis Staff had after its appointment, it could not make any decisions pertaining to the terms of reference of the Executive Board. It could only make decisions from the purview of the Municipal Assembly. But I can't answer that question because I said it already on the first day, that the organisation and the functioning of administrative bodies are not clear to me, and they were not clear to me at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Well, sir, didn't you testify - and I'm sorry, I don't have the page in front of me - I believe yesterday that you asked Dr. Kovacevic to abolish the Crisis Staff so the Executive Board could start functioning? And let me read also -- didn't you say in your summons interview, in the interview --

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: And in the interview that you gave with myself and Mr. Malik in Banja Luka on page 22 -- excuse me, on page 22, line 22, you said: "I don't know. I don't think it did. I think that once the Crisis Staff was abolished, then actually the Executive Board started functioning. And I don't recall any different body between those two instances." So would that be correct that the Crisis Staff when it was functioning replaced any meetings of the Executive Board, that you reported to the Crisis Staff and not to the Executive Board in a separate meeting?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember this interview with yourself in Banja Luka, and I remember that I said that the Crisis Staff functioned and discharged all of those duties.
